content: Rupatadine is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and a platelet-activating factor (PAF) antagonist, primarily used for the treatment of allergies. It was discovered and developed by the Spanish pharmaceutical company J. Uriach y Cia, S.A., and is marketed under various trade names, including Rupafin, Alergoliber, Rinialer, Pafinur, Rupax, and Ralif. Rupatadine fumarate has been approved for the treatment of allergic rhinitis and chronic urticaria in adults and children aged 12 years and older. The recommended daily dose is 10 mg, administered orally. The medication is available in the form of round, light salmon-colored tablets, each containing 10 mg of rupatadine (as fumarate). It is intended for oral administration once daily. Rupatadine is a non-sedating antihistamine. However, as with other non-sedating second-generation antihistamines, the most commonly reported side effects in controlled clinical studies include somnolence, headaches, and fatigue. Rupatadine functions as a second-generation, non-sedating, long-acting histamine antagonist with selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist activity. Additionally, it blocks the receptors of platelet-activating factor (PAF), as demonstrated in both in vitro and in vivo studies. The drug exhibits anti-allergic properties, including the inhibition of mast cell degranulation triggered by immunological and non-immunological stimuli. It also inhibits the release of cytokines, particularly tumor necrosis factor (TNF), from human mast cells and monocytes. Pharmacokinetically, rupatadine is metabolized into several active metabolites, including desloratadine, 3-hydroxydesloratadine, 6-hydroxydesloratadine, and 5-hydroxydesloratadine. The discovery, pre-clinical, and clinical development of rupatadine were carried out by J. Uriach y Cia, S.A. It was first launched in Spain in 2003 under the brand name Rupafin. The product has since been approved for registration in 23 European Union countries, 8 Central American countries, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Turkey, and 14 African countries. The efficacy of rupatadine in treating allergic rhinitis (AR) and chronic idiopathic urticaria (CIU) has been evaluated in several controlled studies involving adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older. These studies have demonstrated a rapid onset of action and a favorable safety profile, even during prolonged treatment periods lasting up to one year.
